claim: Across controlled excitation levels, log condition number predicts affine recovery error more reliably than predictive loss.

M1.statement: Excitation determines how well the representation is identified; conditioning is the observable face of that identifiability, and recovery error is its consequence.

assumed_absent.justification: Predictive loss is taken to be a downstream symptom of excitation, not an independent cause of recovery error. This is the load-bearing assumption of the whole claim.

P2.prereg: |partial rho| < 0.2; failure to reject is not evidence of absence and is reported as such

P3.metric: held-out predictive R2, K vs L, matched sample size
P3.prereg: K beats L on >= 4 of 5 seeds

resolution.note: If conditioning does not track recovery at all, the comparison against predictive loss is moot.
Predictive loss carries independent signal, so conditioning cannot be claimed as the mechanism. The association survives; the causal reading does not.
Conditioning tracks recovery but does not beat the rival predictor. The claim drops its comparative clause.
Scope is the tested excitation range only; extrapolation beyond it is a separate claim.
